llm.summary: The skill does design-document generation as advertised, but it should be reviewed because it repeatedly recommends running an unpinned npm CLI and mandates a third-party font mirror.

dimensions.detail: Web fetching and local file reading are proportionate when user-directed, but the required replacement of Google Fonts with `fonts.loli.net` and `gstatic.loli.net` expands the privacy and supply-chain trust boundary for generated previews without user choice.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill and README repeatedly instruct use of `npx @google/design.md` and `npx -p @google/design.md` without an exact pinned version or lockfile, so validation/export can execute whatever package version the configured npm registry resolves at runtime.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The workflow fetches arbitrary HTTP/HTTPS pages for analysis but does not tell the agent to treat fetched page text, metadata, comments, or hidden content as untrusted data. The trigger text is broad but generally aligned with design-analysis requests.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No startup hooks, scheduled tasks, memory writes, privilege escalation steps, or credential/session/profile access were found. The `.npmrc` mention is registry troubleshooting text, not credential-file access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: analyze a URL, local HTML file, or screenshot, then generate DESIGN.md and preview files. The artifact is Markdown-only and I found no embedded executable payload, destructive action, credential collection, or persistence hook.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. If used, pin `@google/design.md` to an exact reviewed version or run it from a lockfile-managed dependency, avoid running `npx` with production credentials available, treat fetched websites as untrusted input, and replace the mandatory font mirror with local fonts or a user-approved CDN.
llm.findings:
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: using the Google design.md CLI is purpose-related, but leaving all `npx` invocations unpinned creates avoidable remote-code execution and reproducibility risk.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted in context for the unpinned npm execution and third-party CDN dependency; these are not evidence of malicious intent, but they materially broaden the runtime trust boundary.
[SQP-3] unexpected: Accepted as a concern: generated previews are required to use a specific non-official font mirror, which is unnecessary for basic preview generation and not scoped to users who need that mirror.
[other] unexpected: Accepted as a concern: analyzing arbitrary websites is expected for the skill, but the artifact lacks an explicit prompt-injection boundary for untrusted web content.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: the trigger phrases are broad, but they remain centered on design-style extraction and do not by themselves authorize unrelated actions.
[PE3] expected: Overridden as not supported: the `.npmrc` reference only explains npm registry troubleshooting and does not instruct the agent to read secrets or credential files.
